report.answer_text:
On April 2, 2025, which President Donald Trump called “Liberation Day,” the U.S. announced two tiers of new tariffs: (whitehouse.gov)
A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, scheduled to start April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for covered goods from those partners; they weren’t added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
| Trading partner | Rate announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| European Union | 20% |
| Japan | 24% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| India | 26% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| China | 34% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Lesotho | 50% |
The full list is in Annex I of the executive order. China’s 34% was the newly announced tariff, not its total tariff burden. (whitehouse.gov)
Canada and Mexico stayed under separate tariff rules. The new tariffs also excluded some products, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and certain energy products, as well as steel, aluminum, autos, and auto parts already covered by separate tariffs. The rates above are what was announced on April 2; many were changed or paused shortly afterward. (whitehouse.gov)

quotes.text: On April 1, 2025, I received the final results of those investigations, and I am taking action today based on those results.

Sec. 3. Implementation. (a) Except as otherwise provided in this order, all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent.

Furthermore, except as otherwise provided in this order, at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on April 9, 2025, all articles from trading partners enumerated in Annex I to this order imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to the country-specific ad valorem rates of duty specified in Annex I to this order.

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the two-tier structure (a 10 percent baseline rate plus country-specific rates in Annex I, effective April 9, 2025), but no quote states that the announcement was made on April 2, 2025; the only date given is April 1 for receiving the investigation results.
pages.page_reason: The page describes a 10% baseline tariff and separate country-specific rates in Annex I, but it never states that the tariffs were announced on April 2, 2025; the only April 2 reference is to a different order on low-value imports from China.
